business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Physical Consignment of Shredded Non-Ferrous Scrap

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Articles 3, 5, 17, 22); Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971 (Articles 110-118, 137); Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Title 1, Chapter 2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction (Registro Único Empresarial – RUE); oversight by Superintendencia de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed with certified signatures) or Escritura Pública No. ___ before a Notary where real property is contributed (Art. 5, Ley 1258 de 2008)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital; capital subscribed in the constitution may be paid over a maximum deferral of two years; no escrow account or bank deposit required for SAS formation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [SAS NAME]

In accordance with Ley 1258 de 2008 and the private incorporation instrument, the shareholder resolves:

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The authorized capital of COP [amount] divided into [number] ordinary shares is subscribed in full; payment is deferred up to the maximum statutory term of two years. No escrow account or bank deposit is required for SAS formation.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The corporate domicile is fixed at [address, city], Colombia; all judicial and administrative notifications shall be validly effected at said address.

3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: Effective upon Chamber of Commerce registration: (i) Legal Representative, [Full Name]; (ii) Alternate Legal Representative, [Full Name].

Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (RUE online portal – www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three corporate name options through the Chamber's online 'Ventanilla Única Empresarial'. Upon clearance, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Homonimia. Download the certificate and retain it; the name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days from issuance.
required_dossiers: Completed name request form
Valid ID and nationality details of each founding shareholder
Tax/extranet identification certificates of each shareholder (RUT or passport)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for identical or confusingly similar matches, immediately submit the two alternate names; the registry re-evaluates within one business day at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Authentication of the Constitution Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (for Escritura Pública) or private signature certification before the Chamber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the private incorporation document containing full bylaws: corporate purpose, capital subscription, domicile, duration, governance clauses, and dispute resolution. Authenticate signatures as required. If real property is contributed, execute Escritura Pública and ensure registration of the tangible asset transfer in the corresponding deed.
required_dossiers: Draft private incorporation deed or public deed
Valid ID and nationality proof of all shareholders
Certificado de Homonimia (name availability)
Proof of intended registered office address (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies a legal defect in the bylaws (e.g., invalid share class restrictions violating Ley 1258), execute a corrective amendment by private document and re-attest signatures before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio – Registro Mercantil / RUE / Ventanilla Única de Inversión
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed constitution instrument via the RUE online portal or in-person 'Ventanilla Única Empresarial'. Complete Form A ('Registro de Matrícula'), pay registration fees and verification taxes, and pre-register with DIAN to obtain a provisional RUT. Upon clearance, the Chamber returns the stamped certificate of incorporation and the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Constitution instrument (private or public deed)
Certificado de Homonimia
Form A – Registration Form
Pre-RUT issued by DIAN
Certificate of no prior tax obligations for founding shareholders
Receipt of registration fee payment (approx. USD 115)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is withheld, file corrected instruments together with a formal 'aclaración' letter under Código de Comercio Art. 613; the Chamber must respond within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization of Corporate Books and Appointment Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio / Superintendencia de Sociedades
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the company's statutory books (shareholders' minutes book, board minutes book where applicable, and share register) for Chamber legalization ('sellado y registro'). Record the appointment of the Legal Representative and the Alternate in the corporate minutes; the Chamber endorses the certificate of representation upon completion.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Official minutes of the first shareholder/board meeting (pro-forma resolution)
Shareholder register draft
Statutory books (minutes book, ledger, share registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a book or record is rejected for formality non-compliance (improper binding or missing foliation), cure the defect at the Chamber's business registry window and pay the minimal correction fee; re-certification is granted within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal / Secretaría de Gobierno – Inspección de Policía
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the scrap metal merchant registry ('Registro de Comerciantes de Chatarra') under Ley 1801 de 2016, Art. 106. Submit the incorporation certificate, fire safety certificate, facility title/lease, environmental registration proof, and a declaration that all purchases and sales will be recorded in a police-accessible ledger. Obtain the local authorization before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Valid ID and police background statement of the Legal Representative
Lease or ownership title of the physical facility
Certificado de Bomberos (fire safety)
Environmental registration proof (if applicable)
Company NIT/RUT certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is objected (e.g., pending police records or incomplete security requirements), file a 'recurso de reposición' before the local authority within ten business days, annexing corrective evidence and compliance certifications.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía Municipal – Secretaría de Gobierno / Inspección de Policía (scrap trader registry); Cámara de Comercio (commercial license); Cuerpo de Bomberos (fire safety); Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) as environmental authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Vendedores de Chatarra y Residuos Metálicos (Scrap Metal Merchant Registration) under Ley 1801 de 2016, Article 106, together with Certificado de Bomberos and applicable environmental registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) with territorial jurisdiction
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Environmental Registration/Screening (no full EIA required for wholesale consignment of non-hazardous shredded copper scrap); verification under Decreto 1076 de 2015; an 'Aprovechamiento de Residuos' or 'Gestor de Residuos' permit may be administratively consolidated with the municipal registry
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015 (pH 6.0–9.0; TSS ≤ 75 mg/L; BOD5 ≤ 75 mg/L; COD ≤ 150 mg/L; oils and fats ≤ 20 mg/L); fixed-source atmospheric emissions must meet Resolución 909 de 2008 limits (PM ≤ 150 mg/m³ for material handling equipment) and ambient air quality standards of Resolución 2254 de 2017; all outgoing scrap shipments must be manifested to licensed smelters/recyclers with weighbridge certificates

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos certification (fire prevention systems, hydrant clearance, extinguisher placement, electrical plan revalidation); structural load inspection and storage rack certification for warehouse operations; compliance with the Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) program under Ley 1562 de 2012; and a security/anti-theft surveillance protocol coordinated with the local Policía Nacional as mandated for scrap metal merchants.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) — official website: www.dian.gov.co; electronic services are provided through the DIAN Sede Electrónica (successor platform to the legacy muisca.dian.gov.co and catastro.dian.gov.co portals).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent entity forms a Colombian S.A.S. (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) by public deed or private instrument recorded before the Cámara de Comercio in the company's registered office; the company's legal representative domiciled in Colombia completes the mandatory Pre-RUT (Registro Único Tributario) filing with DIAN and obtains the RUT and the statutory NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which serves as the unified TIN and VAT registration identifier for income tax, sales tax, customs, and foreign-trade purposes. Foreign shareholders must submit apostilled incorporation documentation, a power of attorney appointing the Colombian legal representative, and evidence of foreign legal existence; no minimum paid-in capital is required for an S.A.S., though the representative must be a natural person resident in Colombia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or general pass-through election exists for an S.A.S.; the entity is mandatorily treated as a Colombian resident taxpayer for income tax and VAT. Available statutory elections relevant to cross-border structures include: (i) election to be classified as a Gran Contribuyente (large taxpayer) for centralised filing and refund handling where revenue/asset thresholds are met; (ii) election of the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) for eligible small taxpayers with gross ordinary income not exceeding 100,000 UVT, which combines stamp, income and municipal taxes, but is generally unattractive for exporters requiring periodic VAT refunds; (iii) application of Colombia's anti-hybrid and tax-consolidation rules under Law 2010 of 2019, which operate as mandatory anti-avoidance provisions rather than elective check-the-box regimes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) — Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no de minimis turnover registration threshold for a legal entity such as an S.A.S.: the S.A.S. must register as a VAT 'responsable del régimen común' from its first Colombian VAT-taxable transaction, including export sales and export services. Only natural persons may qualify for the simplified IVA regime, and the relevant annual simplified-regime threshold is 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 174,296,500 for tax year 2025, using the 2025 UVT of COP 49,799); an S.A.S. is statutorily ineligible for the simplified regime and must obtain the NIT/RUT through DIAN.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Colombia operates a mandatory electronic invoicing and real-time clearance system. Every 'factura electrónica de venta' must be generated by DIAN-authorised billing software or an approved technology provider and submitted for pre-validation (validación previa) through DIAN's Sede Electrónica or API before delivery to the acquirer; the invoice must include the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica), QR code, and electronic signature. Export sales require the electronic export declaration transmitted to DIAN via SIEX, the issuance of the electronic export invoice, and, for acquisitions from non-VAT-responsible persons, an electronic document supporting ('documento soporte').

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including shredded non-ferrous scrap and recycled copper wire) qualify as 'ventas exentas' at a 0% VAT rate under Article 481 of the Estatuto Tributario. The exporter must be a registered IVA 'responsable del régimen común', the goods must be physically shipped outside Colombian customs territory, the export must be evidenced by the electronic DEX and transport document, and the resulting 'saldo a favor' (excess input VAT) is refundable through DIAN upon documentary substantiation. Export of services is zero-rated only where the beneficiary is resident abroad, the service is entirely foreign-use, and the foreign beneficiary has no establishment or economic benefit within Colombia.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DIAN-approved electronic customs export declaration (DEX) filed through SIEX evidencing the consignment and the ISIC 4669 scrap commodity code
Original Bill of Lading (B/L) or air waybill proving physical departure of the shredded copper scrap from Colombia to the foreign consignee

Inward Foreign Currency Remittance Certificate ('certificado de cambio') issued by a Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary, evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the mandatory repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN and customs authorities rigorously audit export zero-rating and refund claims, verifying actual physical exit, customs declarations, FX repatriation, and the commercial substance of the foreign buyer. Fraudulent, fictitious, or non-exported consignments trigger retrospective VAT recovery with moratory interest and inflation adjustment, the 160% inaccurate-declaration penalty under Article 648 E.T., clawback of refunds through the 'devolución improcedente' procedure, criminal tax-fraud liability, customs smuggling penalties under Law 1762 of 2015, and enhanced anti-money-laundering exposure under applicable Colombian AML/CFT rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (BdbR); foreign exchange regulation is legally exercised through Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, External Resolution No. 1 of 2018, and Circular DCIN-83, administered exclusively through authorized Intermediarios del Mercado Cambiario (IMC) under the oversight of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is convertible on current-account items without prior approval, while capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment (FDI), require mandatory channeling through an IMC and subsequent registration with Banco de la República using Form 4 (Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional). Profit remittance is unrestricted for registered FDI only, subject to tax compliance, transfer-pricing rules, and annual or final dividend declarations; unregistered profit remittances are treated as capital ruch? The principal practical hurdles are (i) failure to register subsequent capital increases, (ii) routing through non-IMC accounts, (iii) source-of-funds rejection by the receiving bank, and (iv) withholding tax and 'no rebuttal' tax clearances from DIAN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian law requires exporters to 'reintegrate' 100% of gross export proceeds from goods, including shredded non-ferrous scrap, through an IMC in COP. The legal channeling window for goods exports is 4 months from the date of shipment when the payment is on a sight basis; if documentary credit or usance payment terms exceed 120 days, the exporter may use the negotiated payment term up to a maximum of 12 months, provided the underlying operation is evidenced by the DIAN Exportation (DEX) declaration and commercial documents. The exporter must also file the corresponding exchange declaration (Form 1) and obtain a 'certificado de canalización' to close the transaction; any un-chanellized export proceeds expose the exporter to penalties calculated under SFC and customs regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account in COP + separate escrow/capital collection sub-account for FDI
Operational account in COP + documentary LC/foreign-trade clearing account
Operational account in COP + trade finance facility account
Operational account in COP + FX derivative collateral account
Operational account + capital escrow for non-resident investment vehicles
Operational account in COP + trade-finance working-capital account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and, for Colombian regulatory purposes, legally non-viable as a primary clearing channel. Colombian exchange control requires every domestic or cross-border payment involving export proceeds, import disbursements, and FDI to pass through a locally licensed IMC. Offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Currencycloud, Mercury) are not authorized to submit Banco de la República exchange declarations, hold COP settlement accounts, or receive export proceeds under the Colombian foreign exchange regime. They may only be used as auxiliary treasury information tools; the actual flow must be cleared through a Colombian Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian SFC regulations permit remote video onboarding for corporate accounts if the bank has secure authentication and e-signature procedures, but for a newly incorporated SAS engaged in metal scrap trading, most Tier-1 banks require at least one video interview with the legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owners. Physical presence at a Colombian branch is not a statutory requirement for a foreign-owned company when a power of attorney has been granted to a local representative before a Colombian notary; however, the shareholder and director must be identified with a valid passport or Colombian cédula, and the company must present apostilled constitutional documents, a commercial registry certificate (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal), and a local tax ID (NIT). In practice, the bank will require a local compliance point-of-contact for the enhanced-due-diligence process and will likely impose a mandatory branch interview, which should be performed by the appointed local representative or a director upon arrival.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company is an early-stage SAS with no operational history and a non-resident legal representative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial registry certificate issued within 30 days; apostilled SAS bylaws and notarized powers of attorney; UBO declaration with names, nationality, passport copies, and employment/professional background; stakeholder declarations of source of wealth; a detailed business plan for ISIC 4669 non-ferrous scrap commerce; 24-month pro-forma financial statements; list of expected counterparties and freight forwarders; prior bank or notarial bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector risk: recycled scrap copper wire classified as enhanced-risk both under Colombian UIAF guidance and international AML typologies due to potential money laundering through commodity trading
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC transaction profile explaining physical flow; supplier traceability documentation including purchase contracts, invoices, weight receipts, delivery tickets, and transport manifests; certificate of origin of scrap; environmental permits and DIAN export registry; confirmed purchase orders or letters of intent from final consumers; dedicated AML questionnaire completed by the legal representative and shareholders; proof of physical storage or warehouse inspection if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI coming from a shell/holding jurisdiction (e.g., Panama or BVI) with no economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registration and tax residency certificates from the investor's home country; audited financial statements of the investing entity; source-of-funds reports and bank statements for the previous six months; organizational chart showing ultimate natural-person UBOs; explanations of business rationale for holding-company structure; sworn statement of compliance with OECD and FATF standards; evidence of registration of the investment with Banco de la República via Form 4.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export proceeds expected under a letter of credit from a buyer in a high-risk or offshore jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully confirmed and irrevocable L/C with issuance bank and confirmation bank details; anti-money-laundering screening for both banks; exporter/buyer contract and final sale invoice; export customs declaration; shipping documents including bill of lading, packing list, and certificate of analysis; bank references from the issuing/confirming bank; clarity on Incoterms to prevent invoicing mismatches.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from the non-resident shareholder must be wired by SWIFT MT103 to the Colombian SAS's operational account at a Tier-1 IMC. The wire instruction field 70 must clearly state 'Foreign Direct Investment / subscription of shares in SAS Law 1258/2008' and refer to the SAS NIT and pending Banco de la República registration. No third-party or inter-company cash pooling should be used; the capital injection must originate from the shareholder's own corporate bank account. The receiving IMC will complete Form 4, register the FDI with Banco de la República, and issue a channelization certificate. The legal entry currency should be USD, EUR, or other convertible currency; the bank will convert into COP at the market exchange rate (TCRM) and credit the SAS account. The documentation bundle for the bank should include the FDI declaration, apostilled board or shareholder resolution approving the capital increase, legalized powers, company NIT certificate, and the bank's own source-of-funds questionnaire. A SWIFT error in purpose code or beneficiary NIT may trigger temporary freeze and SFC reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to foreign suppliers of recycled copper scrap must be executed via (a) documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 by the local IMC using SWIFT MT700/MT707, or (b) open-account bank transfers using SWIFT MT103 with mandatory supporting documentation. For open-account trade, the SAS must provide the DIAN import declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/air waybill, and a copy of the supplier contract; the IMC files Form 2 (Declaración de Cambio por Importación de Bienes) to accompany the payment. For LC transactions, the payment is covered by the LC terms, and the SAS must execute the local exchange declaration within the LC settlement date. All outbound disbursements should carry the correct ISO currency code and the exchange declaration is mandatory even where the invoice is denominated in USD but paid in COP. Taylor-made purpose codes and records must match the HS 7404 customs nomenclature for copper waste and scrap.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/COP spot-forward outright contracts executed with a Banco de la República-authorized IMC, covering the open trade position up to 12 months.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the official TCRM/TRM rate, permitted for genuine trade flows and settled in COP.
Cross-currency USD/COP swaps with a licensed IMC, including FX swap arrangements between a USD operational account collateral and a COP treasury line.
Currency options (call and put) on USD/COP, admitted as OTC derivatives under SFC regulatory limits and subject to KYC product suitability.
Real-money import/export hedging through the use of a forward exchange rate embedded in a commodity-linked trade facility, subject to valid underlying trade documentation and IMC thresholds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Cámara de Comercio of the registered seat (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31; March 31 is the absolute statutory deadline for calendar-year registrants.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Progressive late-renewal surcharge based on average total assets and days of delay; lapse of the March 31 deadline weakens evidentiary standing of the mercantile registration, and persistent non-renewal can trigger Chamber of Commerce administrative cancellation or strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income-Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed electronically on the annual DIAN due-date calendar; for a December 31 fiscal year, the general due window is March through June of the following year, with the exact date assigned by the last digits of the NIT.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of 5% per month or fraction of month on tax due, capped at 100% of the tax, plus moratory default interest; omission or understatement may result in enhanced fines, asset attachment, and administrative collection action by DIAN.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing and Deposit (Estados Financieros de Cierre de Ejercicio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio and, where supervision thresholds apply, Superintendencia de Sociedades; DIAN for accounting annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within three months after fiscal-year-end; certified financial statements must be deposited with the Chamber of Commerce within the legally prescribed annual window, generally by June 30 for a December 31-year-end entity when the filing obligation applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to timely approve and deposit financial statements can result in Chamber of Commerce fines, registry restrictions, adverse auditor qualifications, and personal liability exposure for the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Owner Confirmation / Update (Régimen de Beneficiarios Finales – RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Beneficial-Owner Register, submitted through the DIAN electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due on the DIAN-published RBF schedule, generally aligned with the annual income-tax filing period; event-driven updates for qualifying shareholding transfers must be filed within 30 calendar days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, incomplete, or missing RBF information exposes the S.A.S. to fines under the Colombian Tax Code, loss of taxpayer good-standing, and personal administrative liability for the legal representative.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor / revisor fiscal is mandatory for an S.A.S. when, at the prior December 31, total gross assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.8 million) or total gross ordinary income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.1 million), or when the entity falls under Superintendencia de Sociedades supervision or large-entity IFRS classification. Smaller S.A.S. entities are exempt from revisor fiscal appointment but must have financial statements prepared and certified by a registered public accountant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian accounting under the IFRS-based technical framework of Decreto 2420 of 2015 (as amended): Group 1 full IFRS, Group 2 IFRS for SMEs, or Group 3 micro-entity simplified framework, with legal books maintained in Colombian pesos.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year the S.A.S. must confirm and update its ultimate beneficial-owner data in the DIAN RBF register. The report identifies direct or indirect natural-person owners at or above the RBF ownership threshold (generally 10% or control). Any share transfer that changes the beneficial-owner composition within the taxation year must be reflected in the annual confirmation and, where qualifying, reported to DIAN within 30 calendar days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Acciones)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas)

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (FY2024 and FY2025); 5-percentage-point surcharge for non-renewable resource extractors, not applicable to scrap trading
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New small companies (E.T. Art. 113-1): 0% year 1, 9% year 2, 17% year 3, 24% year 4, 32% year 5, 35% from year 6, if taxable income < 5,000 UVT (COP 248.995M for FY2025) and 3+ new jobs; 50% deduction on investments in renewable energy/environmental control; 100% deduction for approved STI investments
stage_6.tax_loss_carryforward_note: Losses generated from FY2017 onward are technically offsetable for an indefinite period (E.T. Art. 147 as amended by Law 1819/2016); the '5' below reflects the residual statutory prescription applicable to pre-2017 losses and the general 5-year descriptive benchmark in Colombian tax form instructions; Law 2277/2022 caps annual offset at 5% of net taxable income computed before the loss compensation
